The Story of the Frog

I bow to Lord Jina, worshipped by the world, to the word of Jina, counted as supreme, and to the supremely passionless monks, free from faults like attachment, aversion, delusion, and deceit, and I write the story of a frog who attained fruit through worship of Lord Jina.

Through examples cited in the scriptures, it is clearly seen that the worship of Lord Jina destroys sins and bestows the happiness of heaven and liberation. Therefore, those worthy souls who worship Lord Jina with pure intentions for the growth of dharma are true right-view holders and are qualified for liberation. On the contrary, those who criticise worship are sinners and objects of criticism in the world. Such people always suffer from distress, poverty, disease, grief, and other hardships, and ultimately go to lower births. Therefore, worthy souls should always perform good deeds like the consecration, worship, praise, and meditation of Lord Jina. Besides this, through pilgrimage, installation, and worship of Lord Jina — who is worshipped by Indra, Dharanendra, Vidyadharas, Chakravartins, and all great beings — all excellent happiness is attained. Worship of Lord Jina is the cause of great merit, as written everywhere. Therefore, there is no cause of merit equal to Jain worship in the world, nor will there ever be. Who has the power to write the fruit attained by many great souls like Bharat through Jain worship? What can we write about the fruit attained by those who worship with the eight substances — fragrance, flowers, etc. — when even a frog attained heavenly happiness by worshipping with just a single insignificant flower?

Samantabhadra Swami has also written on this subject: 'In Rajgriha, a frog, intoxicated with joy, clearly showed to noble souls that even by worshipping Lord Jina with just a single flower, excellent fruit is attained, just as I have attained.'

Now hear the story of the frog. This Bharatvarsha is south of Meru in Jambudvip. Many Tirthankaras were born here, so it is greatly sacred. Magadh is a famous and wealthy country in Bharatvarsha. It is as if all the world's Lakshmi has gathered here. The residents are mostly wealthy, righteous, generous, and helpful to others.

At the time of this story, the capital of Magadh was Rajgriha. The king was Shrenik, a great devotee of Lord Jina. One day, a frog saw a procession of Lord Jina's worship. Intoxicated with joy, the frog hopped toward the Lord and offered a single flower it had found. Through this simple act of worship, the frog attained heavenly birth and eventually liberation.

This story teaches that no act of worship is too small when done with sincere devotion. Even a frog, with just a single flower, attained the highest fruit through worship of Lord Jina. The wise should understand that devotion, not the magnitude of the offering, determines the fruit of worship. Even the simplest act of worship, when performed with pure heart and true faith, can lead to liberation.
